> I try to design a retractable light saber with an led light that allows for the whole thing to be illuminated and glow. Everything in the project will mainly be designed by me. From what I've seen online from my research is that light saber models focus on either having a retractable blade or a light up one,I will try to combine and incorporate both into this project,I will also add a button to the led++ a hilt cover allowing for a changeable hilt design.

### 2026-10-15 – Now that I was done with the hilt I moved onto the next part of my problem, the retractable blade part. I had a few ideas however I was unsure how to proceed, some investigating later I decided that I

**0.75h**

Now that I was done with the hilt I moved onto the next part of my problem, the retractable blade part. I had a few ideas however I was unsure how to proceed, some investigating later I decided that I would attempt to do a reference model on Tinkercad in order to better understand how the components should be developed for my light saber to do what I intended it to do and move from there 8now would be a good time to mention that I do not have an imagination at all,like at all so a visual model was necessary)  like a rough sketch and move from there.  I considered other retracting mechanisms such as a spring loaded mechanism or a sliding blade (neither of which would work)

However, I realised that since the lightsaber was already cylindrical I could just have progressively narrower hollow cylinders such that they overlap one another allowing for it to collapse or expand. The base of one cylinder will be wider than the tip of the preceding  cylinder which would prevent it from completely sliding out and hold it in place (this is not represented in the Tinkercad). I used Tinkercad so as to understand their arrangement and determine roughly how many cylinders I would require so as to get the length and proportions that I desired.  I wanted to have a rough idea of what I would do and how I would proceed prior to doing a more detailed model in Fusion 360.

![extended](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/90f94a69bf782cbac45f9c5b4691755e9807e34bacae9499dc0961d9a1652123.png)

![retracting view 2](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/7222e3e8a08669f4590486eb6fc80dca370e0bf01736b63bb7d3fabb4eb37309.png)

![retracting](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/SqenJcVsbXusO3XTlgv7F9V5hj45uC1s/f96442c32bbbda82bd90cebdfbca255b064deff55369fa4372fc5c0096067c3a.png)

The first image showcases an expanded view whereas the second and third images showcase retracted views (in the second image the part of the rough diagram representing the sword was extended so as to showcase the components being moved inwards more clearly (this is possible because the black part is not true to size and is present solely to represent the hilt)

### 2026-10-16 – Now that I was done with the modelling and had a rough idea of what I was doing, I now moved onto working on my retractable blade in my model, the blades were hollow cylinders that had different radii

**2.52h**

Now that I was done with the modelling and had a rough idea of what I was doing, I now moved onto working on my retractable blade in my model, the blades were hollow cylinders that had different radii on base and top (so not exactly a cylinder ig). I could not figure out how to get the dimensions right as if I tried to draw a rectangle I would not be able to have the two sides be different lengths. If I took lines the angles would be off I soon realised it was best to draw lines along the axes however have the ther sides be randomly placed in estimated positions (that are not at right angles) and it was fine!!. Made blades 1,2,3,4 and their printable versions also arranged the sword regularly and as an extended version.
